entities.summary: Numidian was a language spoken in ancient Numidia. The script in which it was written, the Libyco-Berber alphabet, has been almost fully deciphered and most characters have known values. Libyco-Berber inscriptions are attested from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD. As most surviving inscriptions are funerary steles with a simple format, only a few words have known meanings. The language can be confidently identified only as belonging to the Afroasiatic family, although it was likely part of the Berber languages, spoken at the start of the breakup of the Proto-Berber language, or possibly a sister branch to the modern Berber languages.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The decipherment of Libyco-Berber inscriptions has provided valuable insights into the Numidian language and its connection to the Afroasiatic family. This discovery has shed light on the linguistic history of North Africa, contributing to our understanding of the region's cultural and historical development.
